origin.fact: One shop's article says it comes from Thailand and Taiwan, while the same shop's product listing says Vietnam.
One Vietnamese article lists Vietnam as its origin.
It is a strain of the guppy bred in captivity for red colour. No named breeder or year was found.
One US shop calls the albino full red a newer colour strain that only recently became available.

looks.fact: The whole body and all fins are bright red.
Males are a deeper red and smaller. Females are larger and paler, with a white belly.
In the albino form, males are red over the whole body and fins, and females are light tan or clear with red fins.
The colour is best judged in mature males, because young fish can change shade as they grow.
One shop judges the best fish by an even, vivid red from body to fins, plus red eyes in the albino form.
In the BDS form, a wider dorsal fin is valued more.

lines.fact: Full Red mắt đỏ: an albino form with red eyes, red body and red fins.
Full Red mắt đen: a black-eyed full red, not albino.
Wild Red: a black-eyed form, described as a deeper red than the albino full red.
Full Red BDS (Big Dorsal): has a large, fanning dorsal fin.
Full Red Ribbon: long ribbon-like extensions under the belly that reach back to the tail.
Fin-type forms sold in Vietnam include Full Red HTD (high dorsal), RB (ribbon) and Swallow.
Albino Full Red is also sold in ribbon and high-dorsal forms.

keeping.fact: Described as finicky and sensitive to weather and water changes. It can go into shock when moved to another tank.
Rated 8 out of 10 for difficulty and recommended for experienced keepers. Avoid strong light, especially right after a move.
Keep the lights off or dim when the fish first arrive, and acclimate them slowly.
Suitable for planted tanks, tubs, cement tanks and foam boxes. Add plants for cover.
Omnivore: feed tubifex, bloodworms, mosquito larvae, artemia and fine pellets or flakes, without overfeeding.
Feed once or twice a day for no more than 15 minutes, then remove leftovers. Change water about twice a week.
Peaceful and suited to community tanks with calm fish.
Albinos see less well, so use softer lighting and plenty of cover, and keep them away from aggressive tankmates.
For albino lines, allow at least 60 L per breeding line.
Foods rich in carotenoids help the red colour, but genetics set the limit.
A hobbyist warns against letting rainwater get into tanks holding red-eyed lines such as full red.

breeding.fact: Livebearer that gives birth to about 20–50 fry per brood.
Broods are 10–60 fry. Females can breed at about 2.5–3 months, about every 3 weeks to a month.
Adults eat their fry, so separate the fry or provide plants and rocks for them to hide in.
Offspring are fertile. One shop says they usually keep the parents' colour.
Albinism is recessive, so two carrier parents give about 25% albino young. Crossing to non-albinos loses the trait in F1, and it comes back only in F2.
Do not cross a full red line with unrelated red or bicolour guppies, or the colour will wash out.
One forum keeper doubts a red albino line can breed more than about 75% true.
Ribbon females are best paired with a normal-finned male.

health.fact: Albino lines are said to be a little weaker than normal-coloured guppies.
Albino lines bred in closed groups risk inbreeding depression. Breeders bring in related albino lines from time to time to keep the fish vigorous.
Heavy line breeding can cause curved spines, smaller broods and faded colour.
Prone to shock from sudden water changes or strong light.

buying.fact: Pick healthy fish with good colour.
Start with 3–5 pairs from a reputable seller.
Prices in Vietnam range from about 30,000 VND to several hundred thousand VND, depending on the form.
For a real albino, check that the eyes are red. Some shops sell lutino fish, which have dark eyes, as albino. Ask for lineage records.
Judge the colour of a line on adult fish.

controversy.fact: A Singapore breeder site warns that some shops sell lutino fish as true albinos, and that mass-market shops rarely document the genetic background.
A Singapore breeder site notes that keeping albino lines in closed groups risks inbreeding depression.
